title: Accurate metering for multi-stage inference pipelines (internal hops vs customer-visible tokens)
creator: Aditi Sharma
description:
Background:
Many customers build multi-stage inference pipelines on Redwood: e.g., an embedding model -> reranker -> shortlist generator, or a classifier that conditionally calls a generator. Internally we fan-out and call several model endpoints; some hops are purely internal (no visible tokens returned to the user) while others generate final text streamed back to the client.

Problem:
Our current metering aggregates token counts per model invocation without a coherent notion of visibility or chargeability across pipeline stages. This leads to two classes of errors:
1) Overcharging: internal hops (reranking or candidate generation used only to select a final response) sometimes get billed as full user tokens if they are counted incorrectly at the ingestion boundary.
2) Undercharging or inconsistent reporting: when final output is constructed by concatenating pieces from multiple model hops (e.g., generator stitching), attribution of which tokens are user-visible vs internal is ambiguous, producing audit gaps and hard-to-explain invoices.

Goal:
Define and implement a deterministic, auditable metering model for multi-stage pipelines that:
- distinguishes internal-only model hops from user-visible output production,
- attributes token counts and cost to the user only for user-visible tokens (with configurable exceptions),
- produces a per-request provenance record that can be used to reconstruct billing decisions for audits and support cases,
- scales to high fan-out pipelines and streaming workflows without adding large latency or memory overhead.

Proposed approach:
1) Visibility flags at request boundary: add a lightweight per-invocation metadata field (visibility: "internal" | "visible") set by orchestration layer. Default is "visible" unless the orchestration indicates an internal probe/candidate request.
2) Token attribution layer: at metering ingestion, derive two token tallies per invocation: raw_tokens (all tokens consumed) and billable_tokens (subset based on visibility and configurable rules). Billable_tokens is what increments customer credit.
3) Streaming-aware finalization: stream fragments must carry provenance headers linking them to upstream hops; the collector must wait for finalization windows (configurable short window for stitching) before committing billable_tokens to ledger to avoid double-charging when the same content is produced by multiple hops.
4) Audit trail: persist a compact provenance entry per request that lists model hops (model name, visibility flag, raw_tokens, billable_tokens, reason) and a final rationale string (e.g., "reranker internal - non-billable; generator visible - billable").
5) Config knobs: tenant-level policy to override defaults (e.g., bill internal rerankers for research customers), and a safe mode that logs but does not charge until a policy is enabled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover pipelines with: pure internal fan-out, generator stitching from multiple candidates, conditional model hops, and failure/retry semantics.
- E2E integration test that runs a simulated pipeline at qps=100 and validates ledger increments against expected billable_tokens.
- Audit export endpoint returns a human-readable provenance record for any invoice line item.
- No regression in P95 latency beyond 2% for typical pipelines.
- Rollout plan and feature gate in place for tenant policies.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spike, 2w): define metadata schema, update orchestration to set visibility in a minimal prototype, and build a replayable test harness that simulates three-stage pipelines.
- Phase 2 (core implementation, 3w): implement token attribution layer in metering ingestion, add streaming provenance headers, and wire into ledger commit path with a short finalization window.
- Phase 3 (hardening & policy, 2w): add tenant policy layer and safe-mode flag, build audit export, and run smoke tests with production traffic shadowing.
- Phase 4 (rollout): gradual ramp behind feature flag; monitor billing deltas and customer support signals.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for visibility rules and billable_tokens logic.
- Integration tests with mocked orchestrator to simulate different pipeline topologies.
- Synthetic load test: replay a corpus of 10k mixed pipelines and assert ledger totals within 0.5% of expected.
- Incidents DR test: simulate dropped finalization or network partition and ensure idempotent commit/rollback semantics.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Additional metadata and provenance increases storage — mitigate by TTL and compressed summaries for old requests.
- Waiting for finalization windows may increase apparent latency for billing commitment; keep window small (200-500ms) and make it tenant-configurable.
- Complex tenant policies increase test matrix and support burden.

Open questions:
- Should certain common internal hops (e.g., lightweight classifier) be billable by default for all tenants? (pro: honesty in cost; con: surprise billing)
- How to handle cross-tenant pipelines (shared internal services) where internal hops are on a different billing entity?

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PIPELINE-METERING-2025
- Spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-pipeline-spike (WIP)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1874

Monitoring and rollout signals:
- Key metric: billed_tokens_per_request vs raw_tokens_per_request (expect divergence for internal-heavy pipelines).
- Support signal: increase in "why was I billed" tickets should trigger immediate rollback.
- Latency: P95 end-to-end request latency and metering ingestion latency.

Rollout plan:
- Start in shadow mode for 1 week for 10% of tenant traffic, surface audit/logging but do not charge.
- Move to opt-in beta tenants (research partners).
- Gradual 4-stage rollout with automatic rollback if billing deltas > 3% for a tenant or support tickets spike.
